ownership_reason: Only the gold forms the UTC instant in the new zone: hop 1 only replaces a null new zone by the default zone, hop 2 only returns the instant for the zone itself, hops 3 and 4 pass the zones and the instant along, and every hop returns the gold's result unchanged. At a daylight savings overlap the local time occurs at two instants, and once the gold has converted the local millis on their own the result has the right local time, so no caller can tell which instant was meant without redoing the gold's decision. The convention is pinned outside the gold: DateTimeZone.convertLocalToUTC(long, boolean, long), which the facade called, converts 'attempting to use the same offset as the original' ('Whenever possible, the same offset as the original offset will be used. This is most significant during a daylight savings overlap'); ZonedChronology.ZonedDateTimeField.set, add and addWrapField convert local millis back with that overload, so a field change inside an overlap keeps the offset (TestDateTimeZoneCutover testWithMillisOfSecondInDstChange_Paris_winter keeps +01:00, testWithMinuteOfHourInDstChange_mockZone 'retain offset'); DateTimeZone.adjustOffset uses it to choose the earlier or the later offset (testBug3192457_adjustOffset); TestDateTimeZone testGetMillisKeepLocal pins the facade's ordinary conversions and its null default. London and Lisbon share their offsets, so keeping the local time of 01:15+01:00 London in Lisbon must give the same instant; the variant gold gives the instant an hour later.
